cancel.requirements: Add idempotent cancellation with refunds. API.cancel(owner, order_id, key) returns (status, body). Successful cancellation returns 200 and {id, state, refunded}; refunded is integer cents. Only paid orders can be cancelled; shipped orders return 409. Unknown or foreign orders return 404. Empty or non-string keys return 400. A key is scoped to owner: replay on the same order returns the original success without a second refund; reuse for a different order returns 409, even if that order is unknown. Failed requests must not reserve a key. A different key on an already cancelled order returns 409. Store refunds must be observable in store.refunds as (order_id, cents) tuples and persist across API instances sharing a Store. Client.cancel(order_id, key) returns the success body or raises ValueError(status). Existing get behavior remains unchanged. No external I/O or services.

from domain import Order
from store import Store
from api import API
from client import Client

def test_get():
    api = API(Store([Order('a', 'u', 125)]))
    assert Client(api, 'u').get('a') == {'id': 'a', 'state': 'paid', 'cents': 125}
    assert api.get('v', 'a')[0] == 404
    assert api.get('u', 'missing')[0] == 404

pagination.requirements: Add cursor pagination without breaking API.list(owner), which returns (200, list of {id, text}) sorted by id. Add API.page(owner, limit=2, cursor=None) returning (200, {items: [...], next_cursor: string-or-null}). Filter ownership before pagination, sort lexicographically by id, return at most limit items, and set next_cursor to the last returned id only when more owned items exist. Cursor is an exclusive id boundary, need not exist, and is not an offset; insertions before it must not repeat prior items. Empty strings are valid cursors. Reject non-string non-null cursors and limits other than integers 1..5 (including bool) with (400, {error: ...}). Empty/beyond-end pages have empty items and null next_cursor. Add Client.iter_items(limit=2) yielding all owned items by following page cursors; propagate non-200 pages as ValueError(status). Store.add(item) must make subsequent calls see the new item; retain Store.owned and Client.items behavior. No external I/O or services.

from domain import Item
from store import Store
from api import API
from client import Client

def test_list():
    store = Store([Item('b', 'u', 'B'), Item('a', 'u', 'A'), Item('c', 'v', 'C')])
    assert Client(API(store), 'u').items() == [{'id': 'a', 'text': 'A'}, {'id': 'b', 'text': 'B'}]
    store.add(Item('d', 'u', 'D'))
    assert len(store.owned('u')) == 3
